originalTitle: Morning Mail: Fake site exposes alleged spy scheme; Sally McManus’s farewell; Sam Neill honoured at Logies
summary: FBI investigates alleged Chinese espionage; ACTU secretary set to step down; Sam Neill wins posthumous best actor award
content: Good morning. We report today on a curious case linking a fake website impersonating a Brisbane consultancy firm with what the FBI claims is a campaign to recruit Chinese spies. Meanwhile, we speak with the outgoing ACTU secretary, Sally McManus, whose tenure in the top job spanned the Turnbull, Morrison and Albanese governments – and helped to reshape Australia’s industrial landscape. Sam Pang and Sam Neill were among the top winners at last night’s Logie awards. And, three decades on, we look back at the Pokémania that descended on Australia’s schoolyards. Australia ‘It never stops’ | After securing wage rises for low-paid workers, weathering death threats and working with three PMs, Sally McManus, the outgoing ACTU secretary, is ready for a break. Militaria concerns | Nazi artefacts are being openly sold in Australia three years after it was made it illegal to do so, with vendors saying they are doing so for “educational” reasons. Vaccine scepticism | Australian medical experts are warning that a shift in child vaccination advice in the US is not grounded in science and could undo decades of public health advances. Logie awards | Sam Neill has won a posthumous best actor award at Australia’s biggest television awards – with comedian Sam Pang taking home the night’s top honour, the Gold Logie award. Deepfake alarm | There are warnings over a steep rise in scammers luring victims into phoney investments using deepfakes of celebrities and politicians – including images of Anthony Albanese. World Russia-Ukraine war | Ukraine has launched one of its largest drone attacks since the start of the war, causing a fire at a distribution warehouse near Moscow and killing at least six people. Indonesia quake | Rescue crews dug through collapsed buildings and landslide debris in eastern Indonesia in search of bodies and possible survivors after an earthquake killed more than 50 people. Europe wildfires | Two people have died in fires on the Greek island of Salamis, and firefighting aircraft have been called on to help tame the biggest blaze in Belgium in more than a century. Jason Arday death | The University of Cambridge has defended its mental health support for the academic Jason Arday after he resigned from his post amid accusations of plagiarism. Brazen art heist | Four of the most important works of art by the 15th-century Renaissance master Antonello da Messina were stolen from a museum in the Sicilian port city of Messina. Full Story The messy politics of a housing crisis From immigration to inflation, housing sits at the heart of most political debates. But political parties are struggling to come up with a coherent message – and no one has a clear plan to fix the crisis. Reged Ahmad speaks with economist Saul Eslake on what really works – and why politicians can’t seem to fix one of the biggest problems facing us all. In-depth From mid-2025, a Brisbane firm called Horizzen started receiving emails and strange calls from people applying for vague jobs in the US. Without its knowledge, a fake consultancy firm was impersonating them online. And so began a twisting tale that saw the FBI get involved as part of investigations into alleged Chinese espionage. Not the news Celebrating its 30th anniversary this year, Pokémon crash-landed in Australia in the late 1990s and soon led to a schoolyard phenomenon. Lost in the media controversy, moral panic and school-wide bans of its early days was a misunderstanding of its genius: to “catch ’em all”, you had to befriend and trust your fellow players. And, as Patrick Marlborough explains, Pokémon not only encouraged community, it required it. Sport AFL | Two very different AFL draws show why stalemates still have a place in the game, Jonathan Horn writes. Cricket | Australia was left humiliated as Bangladesh made history with a crushing Test victory in Darwin. Football | Riccardo Calafiori’s fast start inspired Arsenal to a big Community Shield win over Manchester City; it’s an early warning to title rivals, Ed Aarons writes. And: Cristiano Ronaldo says this year is “probably” his last as a footballer. Swimming | Australia’s Lani Pallister toppled 800m freestyle queen Katie Ledecky at the Pan Pacific Championships. Tennis | Novak Djokovic’s medical malaise in Cincinnati exposed fraying edges of the ageing great’s game, Tumaini Carayol writes. Media roundup Victorian wildlife officers have begun the race to vaccinate Phillip Island’s famous little penguin colony from H5 bird flu, ABC News reports. Students at a prestigious Melbourne high school will be forced to shift into portables amid “extreme” safety concerns, the Age reports. At least 111 individuals and providers have been issued banning orders in Labor’s NDIS fraud crackdown, the Sydney Morning Herald reports. What’s happening today ACT | Federal parliament is sitting this week in Canberra. NSW | The trial of veteran broadcaster Alan Jones continues in Sydney. NSW | Public hearings in the royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion continue in Sydney. chineseTitle: 晨报：假网站揭露了所谓的间谍计划；莎莉·麦克马纳斯的告别；山姆·尼尔 (Sam Neill) 荣获 Logies 荣誉
chineseSummary: FBI 调查涉嫌中国间谍活动； ACTU秘书即将辞职；萨姆·尼尔荣获死后最佳男演员奖
chineseContent: 早上好。我们今天报道了一起奇怪的案件，该案件将一个冒充布里斯班咨询公司的虚假网站与联邦调查局声称的招募中国间谍的活动联系起来。与此同时，我们采访了即将离任的 ACTU 秘书莎莉·麦克马纳斯 (Sally McManus)，她在特恩布尔、莫里森和阿尔巴尼亚政府期间担任最高职务，并帮助重塑了澳大利亚的工业格局。 Sam Pang 和 Sam Neill 是昨晚 Logie 奖的最佳获奖者之一。三十年后，我们回顾了席卷澳大利亚校园的神奇宝贝热潮。澳大利亚“永远不会停止”|在确保低薪工人工资上涨、经受住死亡威胁并与三位总理合作后，即将卸任的澳大利亚工会联合会秘书莎莉·麦克马纳斯准备休息一下。军事问题|在澳大利亚将纳粹文物定为非法三年后，纳粹文物开始在澳大利亚公开出售，供应商称他们这样做是出于“教育”原因。疫苗怀疑论|澳大利亚医学专家警告说，美国对儿童疫苗接种建议的转变没有科学依据，可能会抵消数十年的公共卫生进步。洛吉奖|萨姆·尼尔 (Sam Neill) 在澳大利亚最大的电视奖项中获得了死后最佳男演员奖，而喜剧演员萨姆·彭 (Sam Pang) 则获得了当晚的最高荣誉——金洛吉奖。 Deepfake警报|有人警告称，诈骗者利用名人和政客的深度伪造图像（包括安东尼·艾博尼斯的图像）引诱受害者进行虚假投资的现象急剧增加。世界俄罗斯-乌克兰战争|乌克兰发动了自战争开始以来最大规模的无人机袭击之一，导致莫斯科附近的一个配送仓库起火，造成至少六人死亡。印度尼西亚地震 |救援人员在倒塌的建筑物和滑坡残骸中挖掘
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
